chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Harun b. Muslim narrated to us from Mas'ada b. Sadaqa from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers from Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said:

A believer has seven obligatory rights over another believer from God, Mighty and Majestic: honouring him in his eyes, love for him in his heart, sharing with him from his wealth, prohibiting backbiting about him, visiting him during his illness, attending his funeral, and saying nothing about him after his death except good.

key_terms.الإجلال: Reverence — showing dignity and respect toward fellow believers
key_terms.الغيبة: Backbiting — speaking about someone in their absence in a way they would dislike
key_terms.المواساة: Consolation and sharing of wealth — material solidarity
key_terms.الود: Sincere love and affection — heartfelt warmth in the heart

ai.seo_question: What are the seven rights of a Muslim believer over another in Islam?
ai.summary: This prophetic tradition enumerates seven divinely-mandated rights that believers owe one another, encompassing respect, love, material support, protection of reputation, care during illness, funeral attendance, and speaking well of the deceased. Narrated through Imam al-Sadiq and Imam Ali from the Prophet Muhammad, it was taught as a foundational principle of Muslim fraternal obligations. The framing of these rights as 'obligatory from God' elevates them from mere social niceties to divine commandments.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. Ja`far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Harun b. Muslim narrated to us from Mas`ada b. Sadaqa from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers from `Ali b. Abi Talib (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:

The believers have seven rights over one another that Allah has obligated for them: (1) honour regarding his eye, (2) love regarding his heart, (3) being considerate with his wealth, (4) the prohibition of backbiting him, (5) visitation of him when he is ill, (6) attending his funeral, and (7) that nothing is said about him after his death except that which is good.
